transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-06-10
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luis (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood SE), Claire (Nimbus CTO), Ravi (Nimbus Head of ML), Jill (Nimbus Infra), Tom (Nimbus Product)

Topics: success criteria sign-off, workload sizing, benchmark plan, timelines, security/infra constraints

[00:00] Maya: hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick roll call - Maya from Redwood, Luis and Samir on the call, and for Nimbus?
[00:05] Claire: yeah Claire here, thanks, we'll jump in, we got Ravi, Jill, and Tom as well.
[00:12] Maya: great, objective today is to sign off on POC success criteria and acceptance tests so we have a clear go/no-go, agree dataset and timing. Should take 30-40.
[00:24] Ravi: sounds good, we need to make sure the tests measure both quality and perf, specifically for our clinical summarization flow.
[00:30] Luis: perfect, we'll propose 2 tracks: interactive summarization (real-time) and nightly batch embeddings/search. For interactive: p95 latency target, token cost target, and quality pass-rate on the human eval set.
[00:45] Tom: can you give the concrete numbers you're thinking?
[00:50] Maya: yes. Proposed acceptance for interactive summarization:
- Quality: >= 90% pass rate on 200 human eval prompts (pass = clinician-rated acceptable summary)
- Latency: p95 < 300ms for 256-token responses on Redwood Dedicated (or hosted with dedicated pool), fallback p95 < 450ms on hosted shared tier
- Cost: average cost per 1k tokens to be below $8 (we'll refine during benchmark)
[01:20] Claire: 300ms p95 is aggressive for clinical text, is there wiggle room? We care more about quality than latency but want predictable SLO.
[01:30] Luis: we can make latency a soft and then hard threshold: soft target p95 < 300ms, hard cutoff p95 < 500ms for go. If quality meets bar and latency within hard cutoff we consider go.
[01:45] Ravi: what's included in the latency measurement? Tokenization, network, model inference?
[01:50] Samir: agreed definition: client request receives first byte of final completion. So includes network to the Redwood endpoint, server scheduling, model inference; we will run tests from an EC2 in us-west to match your hosting region. We'll capture p50/p95/p99.
[02:05] Jill: on the infra side we need to confirm VPC peering, KMS for keys, and no egress to unknown endpoints. We'll send firewall rules.
[02:12] Maya: noted, Luis will send infra checklist.

Benchmarks and workload sizing:
[02:30] Luis: For sizing we recommend a baseline run with 1k interactive sessions (approx 10k requests), 512 token avg context, and a batch embedding run with 5k documents. We'll run these under two concurrency profiles: steady (10 qps) and spike (50 qps) to validate autoscaling/burst.
[02:52] Ravi: 10 qps steady is realistic for our alpha; spike to 50 qps covers product demos. For embeddings we need throughput ~200 qps for nightly window, but 5k docs is fine for POC.
[03:06] Maya: noted. We'll size GPU pool suggestions after the first baseline run, expect to propose 1-2 A100-equivalent nodes for Dedicated baseline but can run hosted smaller.

Acceptance tests / go-no-go thresholds:
[03:25] Luis: Proposed acceptance test steps:
1) Run 1k-sample interactive suite with human-eval scoring; pass if >=90% pass rate.
2) Measure latency p95/p99 against target; soft/hard rules per earlier.
3) Run 5k doc embedding job, measure end-to-end throughput and amortized cost per embed.
4) Verify secure connectivity (VPC peering or private link), KMS key usage, and audit log delivery to your SIEM.
[04:00] Tom: for the quality metric, who will do the human eval and what's the rubric?
[04:05] Ravi: we'll have our clinical team label the 200 prompts, using rubric A/B/C where A/B considered pass; we can share rubric doc.
[04:12] Maya: perfect. Redwood can also run automated metrics (ROUGE, answer overlap) and include side-by-side diffs, but human eval will be the tie-breaker.

Reporting format and artifacts:
[04:30] Samir: We'll produce a benchmark report with: raw CSV of each request with timestamps, per-run JSON summary, cost estimate slides, and short slide deck highlighting go/no-go. We'll put raw logs and artifacts in a shared GCS bucket.
[04:44] Claire: good. We need a one-page executive summary for leadership.
[04:48] Maya: we'll include that.

Security and compliance notes:
[04:55] Jill: SOC2 and ISO questions, we need confirmation of audit logs retention and SSO/SAML for Redwood Console. Also KMS integration details; we don't want keys leaving our KMS.
[05:08] Luis: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we'll need to discuss bring-your-own-key options. We'll include SOC2 certs and SOC report.
[05:18] Jira/tickets: we'll attach security docs to the shared folder.

Edge cases and failure modes:
[05:30] Ravi: about quality regressions, how will drift detection work? We need setup so if pass rate drops >5% vs baseline we get alert.
[05:40] Samir: Redwood Optimize can run periodic evals against control prompt sets and issue regression alerts; we'll wire that up and define the threshold (>5% relative drop triggers alert).

Timeline and runbook:
[05:55] Maya: timeline proposed:
- By 2025-06-12: Redwood shares benchmark harness and runbook
- By 2025-06-13: Nimbus shares anonymized dataset and rubric
- Week of 2025-06-16: baseline runs and initial report
- Week of 2025-06-23: remediation/optimization (batching/quantization) and rerun
- Decision meeting by 2025-06-30 to sign off on go/no-go
[06:25] Claire: that timeline looks doable. We may need to accelerate if execs push, but ok.

Q&A / clarifications:
[06:35] Tom: if we can't meet latency target on hosted, will Redwood Recommend Dedicated?
[06:40] Luis: yes, if hosted shared tier can't meet the SLA we recommend Dedicated reserved GPU pool or Private deployment; we also support model variants (quantized) as fallback.
[06:50] Ravi: cost sensitivity: if cost per 1k tokens is above target can we trade latency by switching to int8 quant or smaller model?
[06:57] Maya: yes that's in scope for Optimize work. We'll include quantization plan in optimization phase.

Recap and explicit next steps:
[07:10] Maya: recap - success criteria:
- Quality >=90% on human eval (200 prompts)
- Latency p95 soft target <300ms, hard cutoff <500ms
- Embedding throughput target ~200 qps for nightly job; batch job complete within maintenance window
- Security: VPC peering or private link, KMS integration, audit logs to SIEM
[07:35] Claire: agreed, we sign off on those acceptance tests; we'll send the rubric and data.
[07:40] Maya: action items we captured, Redwood to share harness and runbook (Luis/Maya), Nimbus to provide data and security contact (Ravi/Jill).
[07:50] Tom: let's lock a meeting for baseline review week of 6/16.
[07:55] Maya: I'll send calendar invite and share the benchmark spreadsheet after the call.

Close:
[08:00] Claire: thanks everyone.
[08:02] Maya: thanks, talk soon.

Note: transcript has minor auto-transcription errors (e.g., K-V cash instead of KV cache, Dedicate vs Dedicated) and some speaker label stutters as typical.
